name: AD 1279 Candidate Event

phenomena.details: A smaller, weaker 14C production peak flagged by Brehm et al. (2021) as a candidate solar particle event; sits near the onset of the Wolf grand solar minimum.

impacts.description: If solar in origin, a modest enhancement of atmospheric radiocarbon production; substantially weaker than the confirmed AD 774 and AD 993 events.

papers.title: Eleven-year solar cycles over the last millennium revealed by radiocarbon in tree rings
papers.authors: Brehm, N., Bayliss, A., Christl, M., et al.
papers.keyFinding: Flagged AD 1279 and AD 1052 as two new, smaller candidate production events in an annually resolved AD 969-1933 radiocarbon record; AD 1279 lies near the onset of the Wolf grand solar minimum.

summary: A candidate, unconfirmed solar particle event near AD 1279, seen as a small radiocarbon production peak and complicated by its position near the onset of the Wolf grand solar minimum.
description: Brehm et al. (2021) flagged AD 1279 as one of two smaller candidate production peaks (with AD 1052) in their annually resolved AD 969-1933 atmospheric radiocarbon record. The amplitude is weak relative to the confirmed events, and there is no published multi-archive (10Be/36Cl) confirmation of a hard solar-proton spectrum. Complicating interpretation, AD 1279-1280 lies near the onset of the Wolf grand solar minimum, so nearby radiocarbon structure may reflect a broad decline in solar modulation rather than a discrete impulsive particle event. It is included here as a candidate pending confirmation.
